faq.q: What's the difference between MPH and KPH?
faq.a: MPH (miles per hour) is used primarily in the United States, while KPH (kilometers per hour) is the standard in most countries worldwide. 1 MPH equals exactly 1.609344 KPH. Our speed converter handles this conversion automatically with precision.

faq.q: Why do different countries use different speed units?
faq.a: Speed units follow the measurement system adopted by each country. Metric countries use KPH as part of the International System of Units, while countries using imperial measurements (like the US) typically use MPH for automotive applications.

faq.q: How accurate is GPS speed compared to speedometer readings?
faq.a: GPS speed is typically more accurate than vehicle speedometers, which often read 2-10% higher than actual speed. This difference occurs due to tire wear, tire pressure changes, speedometer calibration, and manufacturing tolerances.

faq.q: What speed units do different racing series use?
faq.a: Racing series use various speed units: Formula 1 and most international racing use KPH, NASCAR and American racing use MPH, marine racing uses knots, and aviation uses knots or Mach numbers. Always verify specific series regulations.

faq.q: How do I convert 60 MPH to KPH?
faq.a: 60 MPH equals 96.56 KPH (60 × 1.609344 = 96.56). This is a common highway speed conversion. Our speed converter uses standard conversion factors.

faq.q: What is the conversion factor for knots to MPH?
faq.a: 1 knot equals 1.15078 MPH. Knots are used in marine and aviation applications because they're based on nautical miles. Our converter handles knots conversions for automotive, marine, and aviation speed calculations.
